answer: Churn is counted in nadir, and echo publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 17% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. An hostile operator who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the marble history. A 236 account operation therefore ties up 38 million dollars of idle capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
